好莱坞电影级军事怪兽战斗短片，30秒，1080p。开场立即进入恐怖袭击，不做缓慢铺垫。整体呈现真实实拍与实体特效质感。一架军用直升机在黄昏时分低空穿越茂密丛林峡谷，机上共有四名成年女性。袭击期间采用具有真实惯性的手持摄影，怪物完整现身后穿插空间关系清晰的广角镜头。低饱和军事色调，自然现场音贯穿全片，紧张配乐在第一次撞击时立即进入。 【预设角色与服装锁定】 - 预设女角色 #1：驾驶员穿着
，始终位于驾驶舱主驾驶座，负责操纵直升机。 - 预设女角色 #2：副驾驶员穿着
，始终位于副驾驶座，负责观察仪表、报告来袭方向与无线电通信。 - 预设女角色 #3：机枪手穿着
，位于机舱右侧开放舱门内的固定机枪位，负责操作舱门机枪。 - 预设女角色 #4：作战队员穿着
，位于同一舱门后侧，与机枪手保持明确间隔，使用独立安全系绳，后续操作备用步枪。 四名女角色的面部、发型、发色、体型分别严格遵循各自编号的角色预设；服装的款式、颜色、材质、鞋履与配饰分别严格遵循相同编号的服装预设。角色与服装一一对应，禁止串号、换脸、互换服装或复制人物。飞行耳机、安全带及武器作为必要功能装备叠加，不替换预设服装。四人全程保持岗位与身份连续。 【0—1秒】 直接切入猛烈袭击：一个巨大的黑影撞上直升机右侧舱门后方的外部机身，金属瞬间凹陷，发出沉重撕裂声。整架飞机猛然侧倾，摄影机随机身惯性剧烈震动。 【1—2秒】 预设女角色 #4 被甩向开放舱门边框，肩部撞上门框，一只手死死抓住内侧扶手。连接机舱锚点的安全系绳瞬间绷紧，阻止她继续滑出舱外，双脚仍在舱内挣扎寻找支撑。 【2—3秒】 驾驶舱内警报骤响。预设女角色 #1 紧握操纵装置，努力修正不断抖动的机身；预设女角色 #2 快速扫视仪表与侧窗，急促喊道：“右侧撞击！机身失稳！” 【3—4秒】 从右侧开放舱门向外看，一只巨大的有翼生物
短暂攀附在舱门后方的机身上。粗壮后爪扣进金属蒙皮，长颈向门口探来，部分翼膜在气流中猛烈震颤。身体位于主旋翼平面下方，爪痕和凹陷清楚可见。 【4—5秒】 预设女角色 #3 迅速转动固定机枪，将枪口压向舱门外下方的生物躯干，近距离开火。预设女角色 #4 紧贴舱门后侧内壁，避开枪口与射界。枪焰短促照亮 #3 紧绷的侧脸，弹壳落入舱内。 【5—6秒】 怪物发出刺耳尖啸，爪子松脱，在机身上拖出最后一道金属划痕，随即向下坠入峡谷雾气。镜头短暂跟随其下落，但不离开机舱观察位置。 【6—7秒】 预设女角色 #4 借助扶手与绷紧的安全系绳爬回舱内，膝盖撑住地板，重新握紧系绳，胸口剧烈起伏。预设女角色 #3 保持枪口朝外，继续搜索。 【7—8秒】 预设女角色 #1 暂时稳住直升机。通过驾驶舱前方偏右的视野，第一只怪物重新展开双翼，从下方雾层中拉起，沿峡谷弧线快速绕向机头。 【8—9秒】 预设女角色 #2 扭头追踪怪物，按住通信键，大声喊道：“它又绕回来了，准备撞击！” 【9—10秒】 前方外景，怪物从略高于机头的位置俯冲，张开的巨翼遮住部分暮光，目标直指驾驶舱挡风玻璃。机头、怪物与两侧崖壁同时入画，清楚交代逼近距离。 【10—11秒】 预设女角色 #1 猛然侧倾转向，直升机擦着怪物的扑击路径避开。怪物外侧翼尖从挡风玻璃表面刮过，发出尖锐摩擦声，留下清晰划痕；怪物躯干从机头侧下方掠过，没有穿过旋翼。 【11—12秒】 怪物沿右侧舱门前下方掠过，进入预设女角色 #3 的安全射界。她再次开火，曳光弹穿过薄雾，其中一串击中怪物翼膜边缘。翼膜出现破口，怪物飞行姿态明显失衡。 【12—13秒】 更清晰的外部广角：第二只怪物突然从直升机左后侧的峡谷岩壁阴影中跃出，形成夹击。它从机尾下方穿过，迅速逼近右后方开放舱门；第一只怪物仍在远处盘旋，两者位置明确。 【13—14秒】 预设女角色 #4 从舱门后侧固定支架上取下备用步枪，安全系绳保持连接。她在预设女角色 #3 后方稳住跪姿，枪口从舱门后半部探向右后方，对第二只怪物开火，射线不穿过队友或机身。 【14—15秒】 第二只怪物被击中外侧翼部，猛然偏转，无法维持升力，旋转着坠向下方树冠。树枝剧烈折断、树叶腾起，怪物消失在密林中。 【15—17秒】慢动作： 第一只怪物调整姿态，从直升机右侧略偏下方再次扑向开放舱门，巨口张开，破损翼膜在气流中撕扯。镜头从舱内看向门外，獠牙与门框之间的距离迅速缩短。预设女角色 #3 压稳机枪，预设女角色 #4 在门框后侧举稳步枪，两条射线保持分离。声音收窄为低沉旋翼声、呼吸与逐渐迫近的尖啸。 【17—18秒】 恢复正常速度。预设女角色 #3 与预设女角色 #4 同时向舱外开火，集中射击扑来的怪物。枪口后坐、肩部受力与弹壳运动真实，短促枪焰交替照亮两人的脸。 【18—19秒】 怪物因连续命中而抽搐偏航，扑击方向改变，凭原有惯性从舱门外侧斜掠过去。它的爪尖擦过外侧门框，没有进入机舱，也没有抓中两名女角色。 【19—20秒】 外部广角跟随怪物失控的轨迹：它向下撞上峡谷岩壁，碎石与枝叶飞散，身体沿陡坡翻滚后消失在植被中。避免血腥特写，以撞击力度、尘土和植被破坏表现冲击。 【20—22秒】 远景：直升机摇晃着转向脱离峡谷，尾梁附近受损的外部面板拖出一缕烟，损伤位置与开场撞击保持一致。旋翼继续运转，飞机仍能受控爬升，飞行轨迹带有轻微不稳定。 【22—24秒】 机舱内部快速交代四人的状态：预设女角色 #1 始终控制飞机；预设女角色 #2 检查仪表后回头确认队友；预设女角色 #3 停火并保持枪口朝外；预设女角色 #4 靠回舱壁，向 #3 点头示意自己无碍。四人呼吸急促，没有离开各自岗位。 【24—26秒】 预设女角色 #1 目视前方，声音紧绷但努力保持平稳，通过无线电报告：“两目标坠落，机体受损，正在返航。”通信中夹杂短促电流噪声，预设女角色 #2 同时持续监测仪表。 【26—28秒】 预设女角色 #3 将舱门机枪收回并锁入舱内支架。预设女角色 #4 扣好备用步枪的枪带，确认门轨无阻挡后拉拢滑动舱门，通过尚未合拢的缝隙最后扫视一眼峡谷，随后将舱门锁定。 【28—30秒】 镜头从机舱后方向前拍摄，预设女角色 #3 与 #4 位于近景两侧，预设女角色 #1 与 #2 位于前方驾驶舱。四张疲惫的侧脸被低斜的夕阳逐一照亮，前窗外的峡谷边缘缓缓下沉，直升机爬升进入开阔天空。旋翼声趋于稳定，画面切黑。 【声音与画面约束】 自然现场音贯穿全片：金属撞击与撕裂、旋翼轰鸣、不同位置的枪声、驾驶舱警报、无线电杂音、怪物尖啸、峡谷风声和急促呼吸。所有声音与具体动作同步，室内外声音具有明确的隔音与距离差异。紧张器乐配乐在首次撞击时进入，随着战斗升级，在撤离阶段逐渐缓和。 战斗中的摄影机震动来自机体撞击、转向和摄影者维持平衡的动作，不能用持续随机抖动遮蔽关键行为。怪物完整出现后，使用清晰广角交代飞行路线、射击方向与峡谷地形。保持真实金属、皮肤、布料与翼膜质感，避免游戏动画感。 全片仅有四名机组成员和两只怪物。禁止角色编号混淆、服装串号、人物瞬移、武器复制、射线穿过队友、怪物穿过旋翼、机舱左右结构改变或损伤自动消失。 无字幕、无标题、无其他文字叠加。唯一文字例外：右下角全程显示极小、低调的“AUQIB”水印，使用 Backstabber 字体，保持固定位置与尺寸，不遮挡人物或关键动作。

promptTranslations.en: Hollywood-grade cinematic military monster battle short film, 30 seconds, 1080p. Cold open immediately plunges into a terrifying attack without any slow buildup. The overall presentation delivers the tangible texture of authentic live-action cinematography and practical special effects. A military helicopter navigates low through a dense jungle canyon at twilight, carrying a crew of four adult women. During the assault, handheld camera work with realistic physical inertia is utilized, intercut with wide-angle shots clearly establishing spatial relationships once the monsters fully reveal themselves. Low-saturation military color palette; natural diegetic on-set audio runs throughout the film, with a tense musical score kicking in right at the first impact. [Preset Character and Wardrobe Lock] - Preset Female Character #1: Pilot wearing, constantly positioned in the cockpit pilot's seat, responsible for piloting the helicopter. - Preset Female Character #2: Co-pilot wearing, constantly positioned in the co-pilot's seat, responsible for monitoring flight instruments, spotting attack vectors, and handling radio communications. - Preset Female Character #3: Gunner wearing, positioned at the fixed machine gun mount inside the helicopter's open starboard (right) door, operating the door gun. - Preset Female Character #4: Combat operative wearing, positioned behind the same doorway with a distinct clearance from the gunner, secured by an independent safety tether, subsequently operating a backup rifle. The facial features, hairstyle, hair color, and body build of the four female characters strictly adhere to their respective numbered character presets; clothing styles, colors, materials, footwear, and accessories strictly follow the matching numbered wardrobe presets. Characters and wardrobes have a strict one-to-one mapping; character swapping, face-swapping, wardrobe mix-ups, or character duplication are strictly prohibited. Aviation headsets, safety harnesses, and weapons are layered over as essential functional gear and do not replace the preset outfits. All four characters maintain continuity of their positions and identities throughout. [0–1s] Hard cut directly into a violent ambush: A massive dark shadow slams into the helicopter's exterior fuselage right behind the open starboard door, instantly denting the metal with a heavy tearing sound. The entire aircraft rolls violently to the side, and the camera shakes heavily with the airframe's physical inertia. [1–2s] Preset Female Character #4 is hurled toward the open doorway frame, her shoulder striking the doorpost, one hand desperately gripping an interior grab handle. The safety tether anchored to the cabin instantly snaps taut, preventing her from falling out while her boots scramble inside the cabin for traction. [2–3s] Alarms blare inside the cockpit. Preset Female Character #1 grips the flight controls firmly, struggling to correct the violently shuddering airframe; Preset Female Character #2 rapidly scans the instrument cluster and side window, yelling urgently: "Impact on the right! Airframe unstable!" [3–4s] Looking outward from the open starboard door, a colossal winged creature briefly clings to the fuselage behind the doorway. Thick hind talons dig into the metal skin as its elongated neck lunges toward the opening, portions of its wing membranes violently vibrating in the slipstream. Its body remains positioned beneath the rotor disc plane, with talon gashes and crushed metal clearly visible. [4–5s] Preset Female Character #3 rapidly pivots the mounted machine gun, depressing the muzzle toward the creature's torso beneath the doorway, opening fire at point-blank range. Preset Female Character #4 presses tightly against the interior bulkhead behind the door, clear of the muzzle and line of fire. Brief muzzle flashes illuminate Character #3's tense profile, and spent casings clatter across the cabin deck. [5–6s] The monster lets out an ear-piercing screech as its talons slip loose, carving one final metallic scratch into the airframe before dropping down into the canyon mist. The camera briefly tracks its fall without leaving the cabin observation perspective. [6–7s] Preset Female Character #4 uses the grab handle and taut tether to pull herself back into the cabin, landing her knees onto the deck, regaining her grip on the tether, her chest heaving violently. Preset Female Character #3 keeps her machine gun pointed outward, scanning continuously. [7–8s] Preset Female Character #1 temporarily stabilizes the helicopter. Viewed through the forward-right cockpit windshield, the first monster re-spreads its wings, pulling up from the low mist bank and banking sharply along the canyon's curve back toward the nose of the aircraft. [8–9s] Preset Female Character #2 snaps her head around to track the monster, keying the comms switch and shouting: "It's circling back around, brace for impact!" [9–10s] Exterior forward view: The creature swoops down from slightly above the nose, its sprawling wings eclipsing a swath of twilight sky, aimed directly at the cockpit canopy. The nose of the helicopter, the beast, and the cliff faces on both flanks appear in frame together, clearly establishing the closing distance. [10–11s] Preset Female Character #1 wrenches the cyclic into a hard roll-and-bank, narrowly banking the helicopter out of the monster's strike trajectory. The tip of the creature's outer wing scrapes violently across the windshield glass with a piercing shriek, leaving distinct scratches; the monster's torso sweeps past just below the nose, entirely avoiding the rotor blades. [11–12s] The monster swoops past the lower-forward edge of the open right door, entering Preset Female Character #3's clear firing arc. She fires another burst, tracer rounds piercing the haze, with one stream tearing into the creature's wing membrane. A ragged hole rips open, and the monster's flight posture visibly stumbles out of trim. [12–13s] Clearer wide-angle exterior view: A second monster suddenly lunges out from the shadowed cliff face to the helicopter's rear-left, forming a pincer attack. It ducks beneath the tail boom, rushing rapidly toward the open starboard door; the first monster is still circling in the distance, establishing distinct positions for both. [13–14s] Preset Female Character #4 unclamps a backup carbine from the bulkhead bracket behind the doorway, her safety tether remaining hooked. Dropping into a stable kneeling stance behind Preset Female Character #3, she extends the barrel from the rear half of the open door toward the right-rear quarter, engaging the second monster with trajectories that never cross her teammate or the aircraft body. [14–15s] The second monster is struck in its outer wing joint, abruptly pitching off balance; unable to maintain lift, it spins downward into the forest canopy below. Branches snap violently and foliage erupts as the beast vanishes into the dense woods. [15–17s] Slow Motion: The first monster corrects its flight path and dives once more toward the open starboard door from slightly below, jaws gaping wide, its torn wing membrane flapping frantically in the slipstream. Viewed from inside the cabin looking out, the distance between the fangs and the doorframe rapidly shrinks. Preset Female Character #3 braces the machine gun; Preset Female Character #4 holds her rifle steady behind the door frame, maintaining two separate, non-intersecting lines of fire. Sound funnels down to a muted rotor thrum, labored breathing, and an escalating, imminent screech. [17–18s] Normal speed resumes. Preset Female Character #3 and Preset Female Character #4 fire simultaneously out the open door, concentrating their barrage on the lunging beast. Muzzle climb, shoulder recoil, and casing ejections look physically authentic, with brief muzzle flashes intermittently illuminating both their faces. [18–19s] Riddled with continuous impacts, the monster convulses and veers off course, its strike momentum skimming it past the exterior doorway at an oblique angle. The tips of its claws scrape the outer frame without breaching the cabin interior or touching either crew member. [19–20s] Exterior wide shot tracks the monster's uncontrolled trajectory: It slams into the canyon rock face below, scattering gravel, pulverized rock, and severed branches before tumbling down the steep slope and disappearing into the undergrowth. Visceral impact is conveyed through sheer kinetic force, dust, and environmental destruction rather than gore. [20–22s] Long shot: The helicopter banks unsteadily as it exits the canyon, trailing a wisp of smoke from damaged exterior panels near the tail boom, matching the exact initial impact location. Rotors keep turning as the aircraft maintains a controlled yet slightly wobbly climb. [22–24s] Rapid cabin interior check establishes the crew's condition: Preset Female Character #1 firmly controls the aircraft; Preset Female Character #2 checks the gauges and glances back to confirm crew safety; Preset Female Character #3 ceases fire while maintaining outward watch; Preset Female Character #4 leans back against the bulkhead, nodding to #3 that she is intact. All four breathe heavily, never abandoning their designated stations. [24–26s] Preset Female Character #1 keeps her eyes forward, her voice taut yet composed as she reports over the radio: "Both targets down. Airframe took damage, RTB." Comms are laced with faint static bursts as Preset Female Character #2 continuously monitors the avionics. [26–28s] Preset Female Character #3 swings the door gun inward and locks it to its interior bracket. Preset Female Character #4 secures her rifle sling, checks the door tracks, slides the side door shut, takes one final scan of the canyon through the narrowing gap, and latches the door locked. [28–30s] The camera frames forward from the rear cabin, with Preset Female Characters #3 and #4 flanking the near foreground, while Preset Female Characters #1 and #2 occupy the cockpit ahead. The four exhausted profiles are grazed one by one by the low-angled setting sun. Outside the canopy, the canyon rim gently sinks as the helicopter ascends into open skies. The rotor hum steadies, cut to black. [Audio and Visual Constraints] Natural on-set diegetic sound throughout: metal impacts and tearing, heavy rotor thrum, gunfire with distinct spatial acoustic profiles, cockpit alarms, radio static, monster shrieks, canyon wind, and ragged breathing. All sound effects sync precisely with actions, showing pronounced acoustic isolation differences between inside and outside the cabin. Tense instrumental score enters at first impact, escalates with the dogfight, and eases during the egress. Camera shake during combat stems purely from airframe jolts, evasive banks, and the operator's struggle for balance, avoiding arbitrary jitter that obscures critical action. Once monsters are fully visible, use clean wide shots to clarify flight paths, firing lines, and canyon topography. Maintain authentic textures of real metal, skin, fabric, and wing membranes, strictly avoiding a video-game animation look. The entire film features exclusively four crew members and two monsters. No role confusion, no wardrobe swapping, no teleportation, no cloned weapons, no firing lines crossing teammates, no monsters clipping through rotor blades, no mirroring of cabin architecture, and no auto-healing airframe damage. No subtitles, no title cards, no miscellaneous text overlays. Sole text exception: A tiny, discreet "AUQIB" watermark displayed in the bottom-right corner throughout, set in the Backstabber font, maintaining a fixed position and size without obstructing characters or critical action.
